title: Staggered provisioning playbook: NA / EU / APAC capacity runway (Q3 2026 - Q2 2027)
body:
Summary

This is a pragmatic provisioning playbook for staggered GPU capacity growth across NA, EU, and APAC from 2026-Q3 through 2027-Q2. It prioritizes predictable SLA-backed throughput for enterprise customers while keeping a burstable pool for hosted API growth. The doc contains three scenarios, a quarter-by-quarter procurement/runway table, triggers for accelerating or pausing allocations, and an ops runbook for emergency provisioning.

Assumptions
- Traffic growth: baseline hosted API token growth projection = 28% CAGR across the horizon; enterprise reserved commitments drive 40% of capacity in Dedicated pools.
- Preferred hardware mix: H100 for latency-critical large-model serving, A100 for balanced cost/perf, L40 for cheaper embedding/transformer inference.
- Target steady-state utilization: 60-70% for reserved pools, 40-55% for shared/hosted to preserve tail latency SLOs.
- Buffer policy: maintain 10-15% burst headroom per region for cross-zone failover during incidents.
- Lead time: procurement and provisioning lead times vary: cloud reserved capacity changes are 2-6 weeks; partner bare-metal onboarding up to 10 weeks.

Key metrics tracked
- Provisioned GPUs by region and SKU
- Average sustained utilization (7-day moving avg)
- 99th percentile per-token latency by model class
- Reserved vs burst allocation ratio
- Cost per 1M tokens (estimated) by region

Capacity scenarios (high-level)
1) Conservative (minimum runway)
   - Goal: limit capital/commitment exposure. Add capacity only to meet hard SLA breaches or >75% sustained reserved utilization for 2+ weeks.
   - Mix: 60% A100, 25% H100, 15% L40
2) Baseline (recommended)
   - Goal: support expected growth while keeping burst headroom. Add capacity on planned cadence each quarter.
   - Mix: 45% H100, 35% A100, 20% L40
3) Aggressive (growth-first)
   - Goal: absorb 40% higher hosted usage spikes and reduce latency tail by overprovisioning for peak models.
   - Mix: 70% H100, 20% A100, 10% L40

Notes on numbers
- Counts are logical GPU-equivalents after accounting for multi-instance and fractional scheduling. They are normalized to a single-V100-equivalent baseline for comparison.
- Reserved_pct reflects reservation-heavy Dedicated capacity; burst capacity sits outside reserved_pct.

Triggers and play actions
- Trigger A: Reserved utilization > 72% sustained for 10 business days in any region -> Action: initiate immediate cloud reserve bump (2-week target) and open vendor bare-metal ticket for next quarter expansion. Owner: Diego.
- Trigger B: 99p latency degrades by 15% vs baseline for production LLMs -> Action: shift traffic to lower-sequence-length shards, enable auto-batching relaxations, spin up 10% burst overlay in adjacent region. Owner: Priya.
- Trigger C: Multi-region incident causes cross-region failover above 20% traffic for 4+ hours -> Action: trigger emergency burst allocation and activate traffic-shed playbook. Owner: SRE on-call.

Runbook excerpt for emergency provisioning (steps)
1) Confirm trigger and collect metrics: 7d utilization, 1h spike, capacity per SKU.
2) Decide short-term overlay: choose L40 vs A100 based on workload mix (if embeddings > 60% use L40 overlay).
3) Allocate cloud burst nodes and tag them for routing. Update routing policy to prefer reserved H100 for enterprise tier.
4) Open ticket with procurement for reserved capacity if action persists beyond 72h.
5) Notify product owners and customer success for impacted customers.

Procurement and calendar considerations
- Cloud reserved capacity: plan 6-8 weeks for contract negotiation and region availability checks.
- Bare-metal partners: 8-12 week lead time; prioritize APAC due to longer delivery windows.
- Quarterly cadence: review on the second week of the planning month and lock in orders by the end of month.

Risk matrix and mitigations
- Risk: Supply delays for H100 -> Mitigation: temporarily increase A100 allocation and reduce non-critical batch workloads.
- Risk: Spot price volatility -> Mitigation: shift embeddings to L40 and enable cache TTLs to reduce token load.
- Risk: Overcommit cost blowout -> Mitigation: use staged ramp with monthly checkpoints and burn-rate alerts tied to cost per 1M tokens.

Dashboards and alerts to create
- 7d moving average utilization by region+SKU (alert at 68%)
- Reserved headroom metric (alert at 12% remaining)
- 99p token latency per model family (alert at +12% over baseline)
- Cross-region egress and cost anomaly detector (alert at 25% MoM spike)

Open questions and pending items
- Validate fractional scheduling normalization formula with runtime team (owner: Ethan).
- Confirm APAC partner MSA pricing tiers and minimums (owner: Sophie).
- Align Dedicated contract cadence with Sales booking windows to avoid stranded capacity (owner: Maya).

Next steps (2-week sprint)
- Finalize baseline numbers and circulate to product and solutions for feedback (Maya).
- Wire up the 7d utilization dashboard and set alerts for trigger A (Diego + Observability).
- Start pre-approval procurement paperwork for NA H100 uplift in 2026-Q4 (Procurement).

Appendix: quick reference run rates (estimates)
- Estimated cost per 1 H100-hour (on-demand normalized): 14.5 USD
- Estimated cost per 1 A100-hour (on-demand normalized): 9.8 USD
- Estimated cost per 1 L40-hour: 4.1 USD
- Expected token throughput per H100-hour (large-40b models): ~4.5M tokens

Document history
- 2026-02-14 created by Maya for initial planning
- 2026-03-09 updated with baseline numbers and owner assignments

End of playbook
